summary.en: Translate constraints into a workable method, prove its key step, and test it against a small reference solution.
summary.bn: সীমা দেখে পদ্ধতি বাছো, মূল ধাপের যুক্তি দাও, আর ছোট রেফারেন্স সলিউশনের সঙ্গে মিলিয়ে টেস্ট করো।

notes: The demonstrated programs use C17; the lesson states their input and arithmetic bounds.

sections.title: Turn a statement into a precise contract
Let the constraints guide a shortlist
Discard one endpoint with a proof
Create cases that attack the reasoning
A familiar technique still needs its assumptions

examples.title: Keep a quadratic reference
examples.explanationHtml: The all-pairs version checks i<j directly. For [1,2,4,8] at target six it prints YES. It is a useful reference for short inputs because its logic closely follows the contract.

examples.title: Use ordering to discard impossible partners
examples.explanationHtml: The sorted version prints the same result while moving its endpoints inward. It uses qsort for compact preparation; the C standard does not guarantee qsort has O(n log n) worst-case time.

examples.title: Change the query, change the technique
examples.explanationHtml: For [1,2,4,8], the prefix example reports six on [1,3) and zero on the empty range [2,2). Pair search and repeated range sums need different summaries of the same data.

practice.title: Check pairs by distinct indices
practice.statementHtml:
Input: n, target, then values (n 0..100, values/target -1000..1000):

Output: Print the prompt, then YES or NO for two distinct indices.
hints: Keep the state convention and stopping rule described in Problem-Solving Strategy.
Read the required output before choosing an algorithm.

practice.title: Search for a pair after sorting
practice.statementHtml:

hints: Keep the state convention and stopping rule described in Problem-Solving Strategy.
Constraints suggest a time budget rather than a correctness proof.

practice.title: Choose a method for 200000 integers when you need to know whether two distinct entries sum to a target.
practice.statementHtml: Choose a method for 200000 integers when you need to know whether two distinct entries sum to a target.
hints: Begin with the state and the input conditions.
practice.answerHtml: An all-pairs scan can inspect about twenty billion pairs. Sort and use two pointers in O(n log n) time under an appropriate sort guarantee, or use a hash structure with expected linear time and suitable collision handling. State how duplicate entries remain distinct.

practice.title: Design a test that catches reusing one element in pair-sum search.
practice.statementHtml: Design a test that catches reusing one element in pair-sum search.
hints: Begin with the state and the input conditions.
practice.answerHtml: Use n=1, target=6 and array [3]. The answer is NO because two distinct indices are required. Also use [3,3] at target 6, which must answer YES. Together they distinguish duplicate values from reusing one slot.

quiz.prompt: What should you settle first for a pair-sum task?
options: Whether two distinct indices are required
quiz.explanation: The output contract determines whether a single value may be reused.

quiz.prompt: For n=200000, which operation count is most concerning under ordinary contest limits?
quiz.explanation: Forty billion ordered pair operations are usually far beyond a short time budget.

quiz.prompt: Why can sorted two-pointer search discard the smallest value when its sum is too small?
options: Even the largest partner is insufficient
quiz.explanation: All other partners are no larger, so none can repair that smallest endpoint.

quiz.prompt: Which input distinguishes duplicate values from using one entry twice?
quiz.explanation: The two equal values occupy distinct slots and form a legitimate pair.

quiz.prompt: What does a disagreement with a tiny brute-force reference tell you?
options: The faster method is always wrong
At least one implementation or assumption needs inspection
quiz.explanation: Reduce the case and examine both programs; the reference can also contain mistakes.

quiz.prompt: What does an accepted submission prove by itself?
options: A formal proof for every valid input
quiz.explanation: A judge checks selected cases; an argument is still needed for general correctness.

quiz.prompt: Which condition permits prefix-sum range queries?
options: The requested aggregate is an invertible sum
quiz.explanation: Subtracting the prefix before the range removes exactly the unwanted earlier contributions.

quiz.prompt: What does the two-distinct-index loop do for a one-element array?
quiz.explanation: Equal endpoints cannot form two distinct indices, so the body never runs.

quiz.prompt: How many unordered pairs does a four-element brute-force reference inspect?
quiz.explanation: The inner lengths are three, two, one and zero, totalling six.

quiz.prompt: What half-open range sum does prefix[3]-prefix[1] recover?
quiz.explanation: It sums array indices one and two: two plus four gives six.

examQuestions.question: State the invariant and justify the time and space costs of Problem-Solving Strategy.
examQuestions.answerHtml:
The invariant is that any still-possible pair lies between left and right, unless an answer was already found. Initially every index is present. When the endpoint sum is below the target, pairing the left value with a smaller partner cannot increase it enough. No solution uses that left endpoint, so removing it is safe.

The symmetric argument applies to an excessive sum at the right endpoint. Equality returns a real pair because left<right. When the pointers meet or cross, fewer than two candidates remain and no solution was discarded.

The pair reference gives an independent route through all index pairs. Agreement on many small cases is useful debugging evidence. The ordering proof establishes why the faster method works for every valid bounded input, including cases you never generated.

The reference inspects n(n-1)/2 pairs, so its time is O(n^2) and extra space O(1). The pointer scan moves each endpoint at most n times in total, giving O(n) time after sorting.

With a guaranteed O(n log n) sort, the complete method has that time bound. The example uses library qsort, whose formal C interface does not promise a particular complexity. If a worst-case bound is required, use a sort with a stated guarantee such as merge sort or heap sort and account for its memory.

Prefix sums need O(n) preparation and O(n) stored totals, then O(1) per range query. A huge value range can make a frequency array wasteful even when n is small. Estimate actual bytes as well as symbolic growth, and include recursion stack or retained output when relevant.
